policies.title: Cabo Verde nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The published foreign-citizen visa framework does not establish visitor admission requirements for holders of a Cabo Verde passport.
conditions: Cabo Verde nationals are exempt from EASE pre-registration; their international-passport holders are also exempt from TSA.

A natural-born Cabo Verdean travelling on a foreign passport, and qualifying spouse or descendant, has a distinct evidence-based exemption; this citizenship evidence is not a nationality-wide foreign-passport rule.

policies.title: Listed foreign nationalities: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Portal Único's current visa-exemption schedule expressly lists these nationalities and their maximum exemption periods. EASE pre-registration and the Airport Security Tax remain separate travel/security formalities, not an ETA or visa decision.
conditions: The maximum exemption is 30 days for AD, AT, BE, BR, BG, CA, CN, HR, CY, CZ, DK, EE, FI, FR, DE, GR, HK, HU, IS, IE, IT, LV, LI, LT, LU, MT, MC, MA, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SM, SG, SK, SI, ZA, ES, SE, CH, TL, GB, US and VA; 60 days for RU and ST; 90 days for BJ, BF, GM, GH, GN, CI, LR, MO, ML, NE, NG, KR and TG; and 180 days for AO, GW, MZ and UA.

Before travel, the schedule directs listed citizens to pre-register through EASE and, where applicable, pay TSA up to five days before arrival. The consular FAQ describes pre-registration as supplying flight, exit and accommodation data for prior security verification; it is not described as an authorization or visa grant, so this policy remains visa_free rather than eta.

The consular portal says foreign travellers generally must pre-register and pay TSA, but exempts Cabo Verde nationals/natural-born persons and foreign legal residents from pre-registration. TSA exemptions include children under two, qualifying official missions, forced technical/weather landings and airport transit.

The exemption schedule says a stay beyond the stated period requires a visa from the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post. The general visitor framework requires a passport valid at least three months at the time of stay.

This ordinary-passport nationality policy does not determine admission for residents, laissez-passer holders, foreign-mission or international-organization staff, refugee travel-document holders, natural-born Cabo Verdeans travelling on another passport, diplomatic/official/courtesy travel, residence, work, crew or transit cases.

policies.title: Listed foreign nationalities: advance visa required
policies.summary: Portal Único's current compulsory-visa schedule says these citizens must obtain a visa at the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post before travelling. The official materials do not establish a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival or eVisa route for this cohort.
conditions: Obtain the entry visa before travel at the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post, then pre-register on EASE and, where applicable, pay TSA up to five days before arrival.

The consular FAQ says visa applications use an internet platform and may exceptionally be made at embassies, consular posts or in Cabo Verde with a surcharge. That generic processing statement does not prove that every listed nationality receives an eVisa, so the classification is not evisa.

The consular portal's frontier-visa statement is limited to citizens resident in countries where Cabo Verde has no diplomatic representation; it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival rule for this policy cohort.

Tourism visas cover recreation and cruises, are to be used within 60 days of grant, permit 90 days and may be extended up to an equal period. Transit visas are distinct, last four days and may be extended once. Official, diplomatic, courtesy, temporary and residence visas have separate purpose and duration rules.

This policy does not override valid-residence, free-movement/agreement, laissez-passer, foreign-mission/organization staff, refugee-travel-document, natural-born Cabo Verdean family, diplomatic/official, transit, work, study or residence exceptions.
